Scope the release dry run's ref check to refs it can move (#290)

tools/release-dry-run.sh hashed every ref of the repository before its
run and in step 6, so a ref that another worktree moved during the run
failed it, although the dry run had moved nothing (TODO 279, seen on
the PR 284 gate). Step 6 now compares only the refs that the dry run
could itself move, read from the main worktree before and after: the
branch HEAD names, or that it is detached; the commit HEAD resolves
to; and every tag and note with its object name. It prints both
snapshots on a mismatch, so the failure names the ref that differs.
It then fails when any ref of any namespace contains the dry-run
commit, which the script records after its commit. A git error in
either check fails the run and is never read as an empty listing.

This narrows a release-integrity check on purpose and needs the
maintainer's acceptance. Step 6 newly catches a commit in a detached
main worktree, and a detach or an attach at the same commit, which the
old hash missed because git for-each-ref lists no HEAD. It no longer
catches the deletion of any ref outside tags and notes other than the
checked-out branch, such as another branch, a remote-tracking ref,
refs/stash or a refs/replace/ ref; a move or creation of such a ref at
a commit that does not contain the dry-run commit; or such a deletion,
move or creation made by a commit hook. The script's header states
that residual. A write that another worktree makes during the run
still fails it when it is a tag or a note, the checked-out branch, or
a ref put on the dry-run commit or a descendant of it. TODO 279 does
not record which ref moved on the PR 284 gate, so whether this change
would have avoided that failure is unknown.

tools/test-release-dry-run-refs.py runs the script's own functions,
before line, dry-run commit line and step 6, extracted by content
anchors, in throwaway repositories in a temporary folder. It runs 25
ref cases, with concurrency modelled as sequenced writes from a second
worktree, 6 cases on fail-closed reading and structure, and 2 that
remove and repeat each extraction anchor and function. Its first
version of 21 cases, run against the unchanged script, failed the
concurrent cases and passed the detached commit; against this change
all 33 cases pass, and each of 14 mutants that remove 1 stated rule
fails at least 1 of them. The release dry run workflow and
tools/run_all_checks.sh run it before the dry run, and
tools/test-run-all-checks.py records the new digest of
tools/run_all_checks.sh after a reading of the whole script. The
workflow header now counts 7 test suites.
